queries: How does INFERNO inference-aware neural optimisation distinguish the objective of reducing parameter uncertainty in high-energy physics from maximising the classification area under the ROC curve?
How do Shapley values based on retraining all feature subsets quantify global feature importance, and what limitations arise from dependent features and a fixed learning algorithm?
How does the MEKD matrix-element method use four-lepton kinematics to distinguish Higgs boson decays from continuum backgrounds, and why are these observables useful for Higgs property studies?

What do the MEKD analysis of Higgs decays to four leptons, INFERNO inference-aware neural optimisation, and Shapley feature selection studies establish about using kinematic feature groups to improve parameter inference rather than only classification?
scope: Semantic literature discovery and abstracts; not a systematic review or full-text validation of every cited method.
bibliographic_rule: Publication metadata is verified separately. SciSpace index dates for preprint copies are not treated as publication years. The cited MEKD and INFERNO journal versions are from 2013 and 2019, respectively.
